native_result.HypoB: The variable is SES (socioeconomic status). In the base background model (SES + family size + sex) SES has a strong positive, significant effect on BA degree completion (log-odds 0.844, p<0.001; probit 0.366 ≈ the cited 0.3636). Adding race dummies and academic characteristics (ASVAB composite, class percentile) collapses the SES effect toward/below zero and eliminates significance (probit 0.126; linear-probability +0.0142 -> -0.0013, p=0.66), whereas family size remains strongly negative-significant and the female effect is unchanged. The cited decline from 0.3636 to -0.2293 (insignificant) therefore corresponds to SES: its apparent independent effect on BA completion is mediated by race and academic performance. The exact full-model figure reflects the study's complete specification, which included a curriculum measure not present in the supplied file.
